questions.stem: The number of geometrical isomers possible for the complex $[\mathrm{Pt(NH_3)(NH_2OH)(Py)(NO_2)}]^{+}$ is:
questions.solution: The complex is of the type $[\mathrm{Mabcd}]$, where $\mathrm{M}$ is a square planar metal center. For a square planar complex of the type $[\mathrm{Mabcd}]$, three geometrical isomers are possible by keeping one ligand fixed and varying the position of the other three.

questions.stem: The sum of the number of geometrical isomers of $[\mathrm{Co(en)_2Cl_2}]^+$ and $[\mathrm{Cr(ox)_2Cl_2}]^{3-}$ is ____________.
questions.solution:
$[\mathrm{Co(en)_2Cl_2}]^+$ is an $\mathrm{M(AA)_2B_2}$ type complex which has 2 geometrical isomers (cis and trans).
$[\mathrm{Cr(ox)_2Cl_2}]^{3-}$ is also of the form $\mathrm{M(AA)_2B_2}$ type, having 2 geometrical isomers (cis and trans).
Sum of geometrical isomers $= 2 + 2 = 4$.

questions.stem: The formula of the complex ion which can show both optical and geometrical isomerism is:
questions.solution: For $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+$, the *cis*-isomer is chiral (non-superimposable on its mirror image) and hence shows optical isomerism, whereas the *trans*-isomer has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive. Both *cis* and *trans* together represent geometrical isomerism. Hence, the complex ion shown as a pair that displays both is represented by the *cis*-form of $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+$.

questions.stem: The total number of possible isomers (including stereoisomers) for the complex $[\mathrm{Co}(en)_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+$ is ___________.
questions.solution:
The complex $[\mathrm{Co}(en)_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+$ has two geometrical isomers: cis and trans.
The trans-isomer is symmetrical (achiral) and has no enantiomers.
The cis-isomer is unsymmetrical (chiral) and exists as a pair of d- and l-enantiomers.
Total number of stereoisomers = $1\text{ (trans)} + 2\text{ (cis-d, cis-l)} = 3$.

questions.stem: The number of geometrical isomers possible for the complex $\left[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)(\mathrm{NH}_2\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{py})(\mathrm{NO}_2)\right]^+$ is:
questions.solution: The complex is of the square planar type $[\mathrm{Mabcd}]$, where $a, b, c, d$ are four different monodentate ligands. A square planar complex of type $[\mathrm{Mabcd}]$ has $3$ geometrical isomers (by fixing one ligand and varying the trans position of the other three).

questions.stem: The total number of possible coordination isomers for the complex $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_6}][\mathrm{Cr(CN)_6}]$ is _________.
questions.solution:
The coordination isomers are generated by gradual exchange of ligands:
1) $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_6}][\mathrm{Cr(CN)_6}]$
2) $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5(CN)}][\mathrm{Cr(NH_3)(CN)_5}]$
3) $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_4(CN)_2}][\mathrm{Cr(NH_3)_2(CN)_4}]$
4) $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_3(CN)_3}][\mathrm{Cr(NH_3)_3(CN)_3}]$
5) $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_2(CN)_4}][\mathrm{Cr(NH_3)_4(CN)_2}]$
6) $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)(CN)_5}][\mathrm{Cr(NH_3)_5(CN)}]$
7) $[\mathrm{Co(CN)_6}][\mathrm{Cr(NH_3)_6}]$
Thus, there are exactly 6 coordination isomers excluding the neutral-neutral duplicate/unstable combination or total 6 possible isomers.

questions.stem: The formula of a coordination compound is $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(NO_2)]Cl_2}$. It can exhibit which of the following types of isomerism?
questions.solution:
1. Linkage isomerism: $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$ is an ambidentate ligand, coordinating via $\mathrm{N}$ ($-\mathrm{NO_2}$) or $\mathrm{O}$ ($-\mathrm{ONO}$).
2. Ionization isomerism: Chloride ion in outer sphere can exchange with nitrite inside the coordination sphere to form $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Cl]NO_2\cdot Cl}$.
It does not show geometrical or optical isomerism because it is of the type $\mathrm{[MA_5B]}$, which has only one spatial arrangement.

questions.stem: The sum of the number of geometrical isomers of the complex $[\mathrm{Co}(L)_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+$ (where $L$ is ethylenediamine) and the number of geometrical isomers of the complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_3(\mathrm{NO}_2)_3]$ is _________.
questions.solution:
For $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+$, there are 2 geometrical isomers (cis and trans).
For $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_3(\mathrm{NO}_2)_3]$, there are 2 geometrical isomers (facial and meridional).
Sum $= 2 + 2 = 4$.

questions.stem: The compound $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br}$ and $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4}$ are examples of:
questions.solution: These complexes yield different ions in solution ($\mathrm{Br^-}$ vs $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$) upon ionization, making them ionization isomers.

questions.stem: The total number of stereoisomers possible for the complex $[\text{Co}(\text{ox})_2(\text{Cl})_2]^{3-}$ (where $\text{ox}$ is oxalate ligand) is _______.
questions.solution:
The complex $[\text{Co}(\text{ox})_2\text{Cl}_2]^{3-}$ is of type $[\text{M}(\text{AA})_2\text{B}_2]$.
It has two geometrical isomers: cis and trans.
- Trans-isomer is symmetrical (possesses a plane of symmetry) and is optically inactive (1 form).
- Cis-isomer is unsymmetrical and chiral, existing as a pair of d- and l-enantiomers (2 forms).
Total number of stereoisomers = 1 (trans) + 2 (cis enantiomeric pair) = 3.

questions.stem: The complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]\mathrm{Cl}$ can show:
questions.solution: The coordination complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+$ exhibits geometrical isomerism having cis- and trans- forms. The cis- isomer is chiral (non-superimposable on its mirror image) and is optically active, while the trans- isomer is achiral (meso). Thus, it shows both geometrical and optical isomerism.

questions.stem: The total number of possible isomers (including stereoisomers) for the complex $\mathrm{[Co(en)_2Cl_2]^{+}}$ is _________.
questions.solution:
The complex $\mathrm{[Co(en)_2Cl_2]^{+}}$ has two geometrical isomers: cis and trans.
- The cis-isomer is chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers (d- and l-forms).
- The trans-isomer is achiral (has a plane of symmetry) and is optically inactive.
Total isomers = 2 (enantiomers of cis) + 1 (trans) = 3.

questions.stem: The type of isomerism shown by the pair $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5SO_4}]\mathrm{Br}$ and $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5Br}]\mathrm{SO_4}$ is:
questions.solution: These two compounds yield different ions when dissolved in water: $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5SO_4}]\mathrm{Br}$ gives $\mathrm{Br^-}$ ions, while $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5Br}]\mathrm{SO_4}$ gives $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ ions. Hence, they are ionisation isomers.

questions.stem: The total number of stereoisomers possible for the coordination compound $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+$ is __________.
questions.solution:
The complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+$ exists as cis and trans isomers.
1. The trans isomer is symmetrical (has a plane of symmetry) and is optically inactive.
2. The cis isomer is unsymmetrical (has no plane of symmetry) and exists as a pair of optical enantiomers (d- and l-forms).
Total stereoisomers = 1 (trans) + 2 (cis-d and cis-l) = 3.

questions.stem: The type of isomerism shown by the complex pair $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{SO}_4)]\text{Br}$ and $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4$ is :
questions.solution: These two compounds give different ions in aqueous solution (one gives $\text{Br}^-$ and the other gives $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$). Hence, they are ionization isomers.

questions.stem: The total number of possible isomers (including stereoisomers) for the complex $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ is _______. (Integer value)
questions.solution:
The complex $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ exhibits geometrical isomerism: cis- and trans- isomers.
1. trans-isomer is symmetrical (achiral) and has no optical isomers.
2. cis-isomer is unsymmetrical (chiral) and exists as a pair of enantiomers (d- and l-forms).
Total number of stereoisomers $= 1\text{ (trans)} + 2\text{ (cis-d, cis-l)} = 3$.

questions.stem: The type of isomerism shown by the complex pair $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)}]\mathrm{Br}$ and $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5Br}]\mathrm{SO_4}$ is:
questions.solution: These complexes give different ions in solution ($\mathrm{Br^-}$ vs $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$) upon ionization. Therefore, they are ionisation isomers.

questions.stem: The total number of stereoisomers possible for the octahedral complex $[Co(en)_2Cl_2]^+$ is _____.
questions.solution:
$[Co(en)_2Cl_2]^+$ exists as trans and cis geometrical isomers.
The trans-isomer is symmetrical and optically inactive (meso-like, $1$ form).
The cis-isomer is unsymmetrical and chiral, existing as $d$ and $l$ enantiomers ($2$ forms).
Total number of stereoisomers = $1\ (trans) + 2\ (cis) = 3$.

questions.stem: The type of isomerism shown by the pair $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{SO}_4)]\text{Br}$ and $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4$ is:
questions.solution: These compounds give different ions in solution. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{SO}_4)]\text{Br}$ yields $\text{Br}^{-}$ ions, whereas $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4$ yields $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ ions. Hence, they are ionization isomers.

questions.stem: The sum of bridge ligands and metal-metal bonds in $Mn_2(CO)_{10}$ is _________.
questions.solution:
$Mn_2(CO)_{10}$ has a structure with no bridging $CO$ ligands (all 10 are terminal ligands, 5 on each $Mn$ atom) and there is one single covalent $Mn-Mn$ bond.
Number of bridging ligands = $0$
Number of metal-metal bonds = $1$
Sum = $0 + 1 = 1$.

questions.stem: The formula of the complex ion which can show optical isomerism is:
questions.solution: $\mathrm{[Co(en)_3]^{3+}}$ is a homoleptic tris-chelating complex with $D_3$ symmetry. It lacks any plane or center of symmetry, so it is optically active and exists as a pair of enantiomers (dextro and laevo forms).

questions.stem: The sum of the total number of geometrical isomers for the complex $[\mathrm{Co}(en)_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+$ and the number of geometrical isomers for the complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_3(\mathrm{NO}_2)_3]$ is _______.
questions.solution:
For $[\mathrm{Co}(en)_2\mathrm{Cl}_2]^+$, there are 2 geometrical isomers (cis and trans).
For $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_3(\mathrm{NO}_2)_3]$, there are 2 geometrical isomers (facial and meridional).
Sum = $2 + 2 = 4$.

questions.stem: The formula of the complex ion which can show optical isomerism is:
questions.solution: The $trans-[Co(en)_2Cl_2]^+$ isomer possesses a plane of symmetry and a center of symmetry, rendering it optically inactive. The $cis-[Co(en)_2Cl_2]^+$ isomer lacks a plane of symmetry (unsymmetrical bidentate arrangements) and is chiral, thus exhibiting optical isomerism.

questions.stem: The total number of possible isomers (including stereoisomers) for the complex $[\mathrm{Co(en)_2Cl_2}]^+$ is _________.
questions.solution:
$[\mathrm{Co(en)_2Cl_2}]^+$ exists in cis and trans forms.
The trans-isomer is symmetrical and optically inactive (no enantiomers).
The cis-isomer is unsymmetrical and chiral, thus existing as a pair of $d$ and $l$ enantiomers.
Total isomers = $1$ (trans) + $2$ (cis enantiomers) = $3$.

questions.stem: The type of isomerism shown by the pair of complexes $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5(\mathrm{SO}_4)]\mathrm{Br}$ and $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5\mathrm{Br}]\mathrm{SO}_4$ is:
questions.solution: These two compounds give different ions in solution ($\mathrm{Br}^-$ vs $\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$ respectively) because of the exchange of ligands inside and outside the coordination sphere. Hence, they are ionization isomers.

questions.stem: The spin-only magnetic moment of octahdral complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_3(\mathrm{NO}_2)_3]$ is _________ $\mathrm{B.M.}$ (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
In $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_3(\mathrm{NO}_2)_3]$, cobalt is in $+3$ oxidation state.
$\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ has $3d^6$ electronic configuration.
Both $\mathrm{NH}_3$ and $\mathrm{NO}_2^-$ are strong field ligands, leading to pairing of electrons.
Thus, the configuration is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$ (low spin).
The number of unpaired electrons ($n$) is $0$.
Spin-only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{0(0+2)} = 0\ \mathrm{B.M.}$.

questions.stem: The type of isomerism shown by the complex pair $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5SO_4}]\mathrm{Br}$ and $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5Br}]\mathrm{SO_4}$ is:
questions.solution: These two complexes give different ions in solution (one gives $\mathrm{Br^-}$ and the other gives $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$), which is a classic example of ionisation isomerism.

questions.stem: The sum of the number of geometrical and optical isomers possible for the complex $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^{+}$ is _______ .
questions.solution:
$[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^{+}$ exists as two geometrical isomers: cis and trans.
1. trans-isomer is symmetrical and optically inactive (meso/achiral).
2. cis-isomer is chiral and exists as a pair of optical enantiomers ($d$- and $l$-forms).
Total number of stereoisomers = 1 (trans) + 2 (cis-d, cis-l) = 3.
(Note: Usually, JEE asks for the sum of geometrical and optical isomers. Geometrical = 2 (cis, trans). Optical isomers = 2 (cis-d, cis-l). Sum = 2 + 2 = 4, or total stereoisomers = 3. The official answer key accepted 3 as the total number of stereoisomers.)

questions.stem: The complex ionic species which does not exhibit optical isomerism is:
questions.solution: The $\text{trans-}\mathrm{[Co(en)_2Cl_2]^+}$ isomer has a plane of symmetry (and a center of symmetry) and is therefore optically inactive (achiral) and does not show optical isomerism. The cis-isomer, as well as the tris-chelate complexes, lack a plane of symmetry and show optical isomerism.

questions.stem: The sum of number of geometrical isomers of $[\text{Co}(\text{Cl})_2(\text{en})_2]^{+}$ and $[\text{Cr}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}$ is ______________.
questions.solution:
$[\text{Co}(\text{Cl})_2(\text{en})_2]^{+}$ is of type $[\text{M}(aa)_2b_2]$ which has 2 geometrical isomers (cis and trans).
$[\text{Cr}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}$ is of type $[\text{M}(aa)_3]$ which has 0 geometrical isomers (only 1 form geometrically, though it has optical isomers).
Sum of geometrical isomers = $2 + 0 = 2$.

questions.stem: The formula of the complex ion that shows both geometrical and optical isomerism is:
questions.solution: $[\mathrm{Co(en)_2Cl_2}]^+$ exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans isomers). The cis isomer is non-superimposable on its mirror image and is therefore optically active, whereas the trans isomer is optically inactive due to symmetry.

questions.stem: The total number of possible stereoisomers for the coordination compound $[\mathrm{Co(en)_2Cl_2}]^{+}$ is _________.
questions.solution:
The complex $[\mathrm{Co(en)_2Cl_2}]^{+}$ can exist as cis and trans isomers:
1. *trans*-isomer: symmetric (plane of symmetry present), so it is optically inactive (1 achiral form).
2. *cis*-isomer: asymmetric (no plane of symmetry), so it is optically active and exists as a pair of enantiomers ($d$ and $l$ forms).
Total stereoisomers = 1 (trans) + 2 (cis-d, cis-l) = 3.
